title: A trained PINN equals the true SIR trajectory

dictionary.Res0: The ODE residual of the trained network is zero on the whole time interval
dictionary.IC: The network satisfies the initial conditions
dictionary.Solves: The network solves the SIR initial value problem
dictionary.Uniq: The SIR initial value problem has a unique solution
dictionary.Equal: The trained network equals the true SIR trajectory

premises.text: If the residual vanishes on the whole interval and the initial conditions hold, the network solves the initial value problem.
If the network solves the initial value problem and that problem has a unique solution, the network equals the true trajectory.
Training drove the residual to zero.

conclusion.text: The trained network equals the true SIR trajectory.

derivation.statement: Residual is zero and initial conditions hold.
The network equals the true trajectory.

hidden_assumptions: Step 3 needs uniqueness of the solution (Uniq), which no premise states.
P3 silently upgrades 'the residual is small at the collocation points' to 'the residual is zero on the whole interval' (quantifier slip).

soundness.comment: True by definition of a solution of the IVP.
Two solutions of a uniquely solvable IVP coincide.
Training only makes the residual small at collocation points ([[pinn-residuals-are-enforced-only-at-collocation-points]]); zero on the interval is not established.
Enforced by the initial-condition loss up to optimisation error.

informal_verdict: The derivation uses uniqueness at step 3 without a premise for it, so as stated the argument is invalid; it becomes valid once uniqueness is added, but its soundness still depends on P3.
